passages.provision_quote: Any sentence enhancement that was imposed prior to January 1, 2018, pursuant to Section 11370.2 of the Health and Safety Code, except for any enhancement imposed for a prior conviction of violating or conspiring to violate Section 11380 of the Health and Safety Code is legally invalid.
passages.note: Retroactively invalidates specified sentencing enhancements and requires resentencing to a lesser term unless public safety would be endangered, showing leniency direction but no single rung's exact philosophy.

rows.reasoning: Allen authored SB 483 (2021-2022), which declares certain prior sentencing enhancements 'legally invalid' and requires courts to resentence affected individuals to a lesser term unless continued incarceration is needed for public safety. This shows movement away from 'impose the toughest penalties the law allows' but does not establish, clause for clause, whether Allen holds a treatment-focused, restitution-focused, or case-by-case philosophy for how the system should respond when someone breaks the law.
needs_source: A first-person statement or floor speech by Allen describing his general philosophy on sentencing/punishment vs. treatment, to distinguish among rungs 1-3
